findings: The headline as printed (l.2363) is supported only in DEC-28's Cauchy-compact form: Barbot's equality D(reg M~) = Omega needs absolute maximality of Reg M (Barbot Rem 8.13 / Sec. 11.3), obtained here from B21 Cor 2.18; with Cauchy-maximality alone Barbot gives only D(reg M~) inside Omega (WP-41m's package).

The display l.2369 'D(M~) = bigcap_i J+(Delta_i) cup bigcap_{j in I} I+(Pi_j)' is wrong (D-12 (c)); the proof (l.2386-2388) establishes (bigcup_i Delta_i) cup bigcap_{j in J} I+(Pi_j); the regular half is certified here as D(Reg M~) = Omega+(Lambda) = bigcap_{w in Lambda} I+(Pi_w), with equality.

'Up to time reversal' (l.2365) is replaced by the future case (DEC-77 (a)): the formal statement concludes Omega+ and proves the selection in GX.e0RegM_range_not_subset_omegaMinus; the paper's proof never argues it (D-11 (d)).

DEC-76's 'pi1 non-abelian' does not suffice algebraically for the loxodromic element (WP-41m's counterexample GX.exists_nonabelian_subgroup_noLox); the statement uses 'pi1(Reg M) not metabelian', which agrees with non-abelian for the free pi1 of a punctured surface (not formalized).

Barbot's GH of the quotient Gamma\Omega^- in the past case is obtained without Benoist (Causal.Flat.Lox.bcor_loxo_proper_both from the loxodromic element), so the equality of the regular part holds in both time orientations.

The future-case selection (DEC-77 (a), never argued in the paper, D-11 (d)) has a short proof that needs neither the developing map extended to sing M~ nor the parabolic holonomy of the loop around a BTZ line: in the past case D(Reg M~) = Omega^-(Lambda) is past complete; along the radial segment c(s) = (tau_1 + s, s), s -> 0+, into a BTZ point x (paper coordinates of the chart at x), D = g . chartMap on the lifted sector, so the lifts develop to g.(tau_1+s, tau_1, 0) -> p = g.(tau_1, tau_1, 0) in J^-(D z~) inside Omega^- = D(Reg M~); D being an open embedding, the lifts converge in Reg M~, so x would be regular. Formalized as GX.false_of_sing_of_pastComplete (0 sorry, standard axioms, no GH/Cauchy hypothesis).
questions: The BTZ half (D on sing M~, the rays Delta_i in the boundary of Omega, M = rho\D(M~) for the BTZ topology) needs a bridge between the two presentations of an E0-manifold in the scaffold: ChartedSpace E0Y M (where Cauchy-compactness, Cauchy-maximality and AbsMax of Reg M live: AbsMax, Surgery, Holonomy) and SingularGXStructure + MaxBranchedCover (where M~, T_BTZ and D live: VirtTame, Manifolds), plus reg M~ = universal cover of Reg M. Should a package build that bridge, or should the headline be re-read on Reg M only (as certified here)?

DEC-76 reads 'pi1(Sigma minus sing) non-abelian'. The formal hypothesis is 'pi1(Reg M) (the deck group of Reg M's universal cover) NOT METABELIAN', because non-abelian does not give a loxodromic element algebraically (WP-41m's GX.exists_nonabelian_subgroup_noLox). Geometrically the two agree (pi1 of a punctured closed surface is free, and a non-abelian free group is not metabelian), but that equivalence is not formalized. Ruling requested: (a) accept 'pi1(Reg M) not metabelian' as the formal reading of DEC-76, or (b) require the equivalence to be built (pi1(Reg M) free, from the surface classification of a Cauchy surface of Reg M), so that 'non-abelian' is the hypothesis.

findings: As printed the proposition is false (D-11, DEC-77). The counterexample is BUILT, 0 sorry, standard axioms only: GX.e0PastHalf_counterexample. The past half {tau<0} of E0 (GX.e0PastHalf, an open subset of Y = M + E0, hence an E0-manifold) is globally hyperbolic (GX.e0PastHalf_globallyHyperbolic: its charted causality is E0's restricted to {tau<0}, diamonds are closed and bounded by dist <= 3 Delta tau) and has BTZ points (GX.e0PastHalf_sing_nonempty); for EVERY developing pair (D, rho) of Reg {tau<0} and EVERY z, D(I+(z)) != I+(D z) (GX.e0PastHalf_not_isFutureComplete), so Reg {tau<0}~ is not future complete. Proof: r = t - x read through D is globally affine on the universal cover (GX.pastHalf_rad_locally + GX.exists_affine_eq_of_locally); along I+(z) r increases strictly and stays below r(z) - 2 tau(z) because tau < 0 (E0.calculus_lt), while an affine function is unbounded on the timelike ray D z + t e0. The printed Cauchy-completeness hypothesis of {tau<0} (the plane {tau = -1} with dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2, DEC-31) is NOT stated in Lean: the scaffold has no DEC-31 predicate for E0-manifolds (the induced length structure across BTZ lines is GXScaffold.BTZ.Surgery's obstruction (3)). Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete of Reg {tau<0} is not the paper's hypothesis, and we expect it to FAIL (no cusp surgery below tau = 0), which is consistent with B21 Thm 3 needing Cauchy-maximality (GX.E0Surgery.regM_isCauchyComplete carries hmax). {tau<0} is also not Cauchy-maximal ({tau<0} into E0 is a Cauchy embedding) and pi1(Reg {tau<0}) = Z is abelian (both not formalized).

The conclusion is certified for the regular part only (a restriction of the CONCLUSION, not a hypothesis): for every developing pair of Reg M and every z in the universal cover of Reg M, D(J+(z)) = J+(D z) and D(I+(z)) = I+(D z) (the proof's first step, l.2350); future completeness at the BTZ points of M~ (def:manifold_future_complete_all over M~ with T_BTZ) is not formalized.

The proof cites 'Lemma 2.4 of brunswic2021cauchy' for the full future BTZ rays (l.2352); the result is B21 Lemma 2.3 (D-11 (b)); this step (future completeness at the BTZ points) is not formalized here.

The proof's 'from Theorem 3 ... the regular part is globally hyperbolic and Cauchy-complete. Barbot ... implies future completeness of the regular part' (l.2350) omits that Barbot's future completeness needs equality D(reg M~) = Omega+, i.e. absolute maximality (Cauchy-maximality and Cauchy-compactness, B21 Cor 2.18) and the future case.
questions: The printed hypothesis 'Cauchy-complete' (DEC-31: the Cauchy surface complete for its induced length metric, extended across the BTZ lines) has no Lean predicate for E0-manifolds in the scaffold, so the counterexample's Cauchy-completeness is stated in prose only. Should a package define the DEC-31 predicate for E0-manifolds (and prove it for {tau<0}), or is the counterexample accepted with GH + BTZ points + failure of the conclusion?

kb_proposals: Barbot's equality for ANY absolutely maximal flat spacetime with (CC') and a loxodromic element, in both time orientations and with the quotient isometry M = rho(Gamma)\Omega, is GX.uniformization_of_absMax (0 sorry): Causal.Flat.Lox.bcor_loxo_proper_both supplies the GH presentation B of Gamma\Omega(S~) and range_eq_omegaS_of_absMax the equality; no Benoist needed.
Causal.Flat.Lox.PastProper is not in the import closure of Classification/Loxodromic: import it explicitly for bcor_loxo_proper_both.
DiscreteTopology rho.range needs `open scoped Causal.Flat` (the isomTopology instance), allowed under DEC-33.

An open subset of Y = M + E0 contained in the inr part is an E0-manifold whose paperChart has source univ (GX.chartSource_paperChart_pastHalf); then GX.E0CBG.chartIso_paperChart with U = top makes its charted causality E0's restricted relation, and E0's curve-defined le on an open set containing {tau < tau(y)} is the global one (GX.e0_le_of_le_top_of_fst_neg).

The functional t - x of Minkowski reads r off the paper's developing map (GX.minkTMinusX_btzPaperDev); since every BTZE0 a.e.-atlas chart is locally g . chartMap (GX.pastHalf_aeChart_eventually), r is locally affine in any developing map of a regular part, and GX.exists_affine_eq_of_locally globalises it on the (preconnected) universal cover. This affine-invariant trick avoids building the developing map explicitly.

The scaffold has two presentations of an E0-manifold (ChartedSpace E0Y vs SingularGXStructure/MaxBranchedCover) with no bridge: the BTZ half of the gx headline (D on sing M~, rays Delta_i, M = rho\D(M~)) is still blocked on it; the future-case selection is NOT (WP-43f).

To read the developing map of Reg M~ near a BTZ point: GX.dev_eventually_chartMap_sector (locally D = g . chartMap y0 . paperOfY . chartAt E0Y x, for any fixed sector base y0) + GX.exists_isom_eq_of_locally (one g on a preconnected open set, D open) on the connected component of the lifted sector; lifts of a segment come from IsCoveringMap.liftPath (Causal.Flat.isCoveringMap_flatCover_proj) and IsPreconnected.subset_connectedComponentIn.

GX.false_of_sing_of_pastComplete: a BTZ point forbids any injective developing map of Reg M~ with past-complete image; the limit-point argument (open embedding D + Hausdorff M) replaces 'D-hat(x) fixed by the parabolic holonomy'.
